# devdb command reference

<!-- Generated by `go run ./cmd/gen-docs`. Do not edit by hand; regenerate instead. -->

Queryable per-project memory for codebases. Use 'devdb help <command> --examples' to see real command shapes and known gotchas for any verb.

Every verb below is registered by the binary. Flags are listed with their defaults; global flags are accepted by every command.

## Usage

```text
devdb [global flags] <noun> <verb> [subverb] [flags] [args]
```

Run `devdb <noun> --help` for the verbs a noun accepts, and `devdb help <noun> <verb> --examples` for real command shapes plus known gotchas.

## devdb archive

Archive historical ledger rows

| Verb | Summary |
|---|---|
| `gc` | Prune stale open feedback and old dismissed reminders/tasks |
| `list` | List archive entries |
| `restore` | Restore rows from archive_entries |
| `run` | Move closed/resolved rows into archive_entries |
| `show` | Show one archived row with its payload |

#### `devdb archive gc`

Closes open feedback older than --older-than days, except rows whose severity is protected (default: high,critical — stale high-severity rows are live debt, not silt). Use --keep-severity to change the protected set; --keep-severity "" protects nothing (legacy behavior). Dry-run lists the affected row ids.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | false | preview without writing |
| `--keep-severity` | high,critical | comma-separated severities gc never closes ("" = protect nothing) |
| `--older-than` | 30 | age threshold in days |

#### `devdb archive list`

List archive entries

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--limit` | 50 | max rows |
| `--since` | — | archived_at >= ISO timestamp |
| `--table` | — | filter by source table |
| `--until` | — | archived_at <= ISO timestamp |

#### `devdb archive restore`

Restore rows from archive_entries

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id` | — | archive entry id |
| `--keep-archive` | false | leave archive row after restore |
| `--since` | — | archived_at >= ISO timestamp |
| `--source-id` | — | filter source id |
| `--source-table` | — | filter source table |
| `--table` | — | alias for --source-table |
| `--until` | — | archived_at <= ISO timestamp |

#### `devdb archive run`

Move closed/resolved rows into archive_entries

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | false | preview without writing |
| `--keep-snapshots` | 3 | loc_snapshots retention count |
| `--session-hours` | 24 | keep rows from the last N hours |
| `--table` | — | scope to one source table |
| `--vacuum` | false | VACUUM after archive |
| `--yes` | false | skip confirmation |

Examples:

```bash
devdb archive run --dry-run            # preview what would move
devdb archive run --yes                # actually archive
devdb archive run --yes --vacuum       # archive + reclaim freed pages

Non-interactive by design: --yes suppresses the confirmation prompt,
--json is machine-readable. Cron entry:

  0 3 * * 0  cd /path/to/repo && devdb archive run --yes --json >> .devdb/archive.log 2>&1
```

#### `devdb archive show`

```text
show ID
```

Show one archived row with its payload

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--source-id` | — | source row id to look up |
| `--table` | — | source table (with --source-id instead of an id) |

## devdb feedback

Feedback and observations

| Verb | Summary |
|---|---|
| `add` | Log feedback |
| `annotate` | Append annotation to feedback context |
| `close` | Close feedback |
| `list` | List feedback |
| `severity` | Re-seed a feedback row's severity (records are not debt) |
| `show` | Show one feedback row |

#### `devdb feedback add`

```text
add NOTE
```

Log feedback

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--allow-duplicate` | false | insert even when an equivalent entry already exists |
| `--category` | — | feedback category |
| `--context` | — | optional context |
| `--role` | — | user\|model\|codebase |
| `--severity` | — | info\|low\|med\|high\|critical |

#### `devdb feedback annotate`

```text
annotate ID NOTE
```

Append annotation to feedback context

#### `devdb feedback close`

```text
close ID
```

Close feedback

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--proposed-fix` | — | how it was addressed |

Examples:

```bash
devdb feedback close <id> --proposed-fix "Resolved by <commit> which adds <artifact>: <one-line description>"

Name the commit + the artifact, not the closing agent's behavior. See
skills/devdb/SKILL.md "Closing feedback — name the artifact, not the behavior".
```

#### `devdb feedback list`

List feedback, optionally narrowed by status, category, severity, role,
or --context (substring match on the context column).

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--category` | — | filter by exact category |
| `--context` | — | substring match on the context column |
| `--limit` | 0 | max rows (default 20; --all expands) |
| `--role` | — | filter by role (user\|model\|codebase) |
| `--severity` | — | filter by severity (info\|low\|med\|high\|critical) |
| `--status` | open | filter by status (open\|closed\|all) |

Examples:

```bash
devdb feedback list --json                       # stable: returns [] on empty, never null
devdb feedback list --status open --json            # default status filter
devdb feedback list --status bogus                   # ERROR: --status: invalid value "bogus" (allowed: open, closed, all)

Empty --json output is always an array, so agents can iterate without a
nil-guard. Bogus filter values surface as explicit errors (exit code
ExitUsage) rather than silently producing an empty result. See feedback
[654b7b3e] for the original DX complaint.
```

#### `devdb feedback severity`

```text
severity ID LEVEL
```

Sets a feedback row's severity to LEVEL (info|low|med|high|critical) and appends an auditable '[severity <ts>] old -> new: reason' stamp to the row's context. Use when a high/critical row turns out to be an evidence or state record rather than actionable defect — the severity contract reserves high/critical for rows where an artifact must still change.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--reason` | — | why the severity changed (recorded in context) |

#### `devdb feedback show`

```text
show ID
```

Show one feedback row

## `devdb help`

```text
help [command]
```

devdb help <noun> <verb>             # standard help for one verb
devdb help <noun> <verb> --examples  # real command shapes + gotchas

Pass --examples after the verb name to print a curated example block
instead of the standard flag listing. Examples live in
internal/cli/commands.go (examplesByCommand) and are added when a verb
has a non-obvious gotcha worth remembering.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--examples` | false | print curated example block instead of standard help |

Examples:

```bash
devdb help plan reconcile                # standard help for one verb
devdb help plan reconcile --examples     # real command shapes + gotchas
devdb help feedback close --examples     # artifact-naming template for --proposed-fix
devdb help archive run --examples        # cron-safe hygiene command
devdb help ledger housekeeping --examples
```

#### `devdb hub doctor`

Diagnoses registered projects (freshness, hub status, sync errors). With --scan DIR[,DIR...] also walks those directories for .devdb/development.db repos missing from the registry — audit and dashboards only see registered repos, so an unregistered ledger is invisible debt. Fix: devdb hub register --auto --scope DIR.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project` | — | filter to one alias or path |
| `--scan` | — | comma-separated directories to walk for unregistered .devdb repos |

## devdb ledger

Bundled hygiene operations on the devdb ledger

| Verb | Summary |
|---|---|
| `housekeeping` | Bundled hygiene: archive run --yes, plan reconcile --apply, inventory scan, optional verify query |

#### `devdb ledger housekeeping`

Bundles the recurring hygiene steps into one command so weekly cron
entries and end-of-session agents do not hand-craft the sequence.

Steps (in order):
  1. archive run     — archive closed/resolved rows (skipped under --dry-run)
  2. plan reconcile  — detect and repair plan-tree drift
  3. inventory scan  — refresh repo_files (skipped under --dry-run)
  4. verify query    — only when both --verify-command and --verify-scope are set

Cron-safe: non-interactive, --json machine-readable, --dry-run previews.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | false | preview without writing |
| `--scan-paths` | [] | limit inventory scan to specific paths (default: whole repo) |
| `--verify-command` | — | verification command string (optional; runs verify query when set) |
| `--verify-scope` | — | verification scope (used with --verify-command) |

Examples:

```bash
devdb ledger housekeeping                 # run archive + reconcile + inventory scan + verify query
devdb ledger housekeeping --dry-run       # preview without writing
devdb ledger housekeeping --json          # machine-readable output

Bundles the recurring hygiene steps (archive run --yes, plan reconcile
--apply, inventory scan, verify query summary) into one command so the
weekly cron and end-of-session agents do not hand-craft the sequence.
```


| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--body` | — | plan body |

#### `devdb plan delete`

```text
delete SLUG_OR_ID
```

Removes the plan cascade in one transaction (acceptance criteria, item files, status log, items, milestones, then the plan). Refuses when items are in_progress unless --force. Preview with --dry-run: prints the cascade counts without writing. Replaces the hand-ordered raw-SQL cascade recipe (skill pitfall 10).

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | false | preview cascade counts without writing |
| `--force` | false | delete even when items are in_progress |

#### `devdb plan list`

List plans

#### `devdb plan promote`

Promote design-scaffolded items to implement mode

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--plan` | — | plan slug or id |

#### `devdb plan reconcile`

Detect or repair plan-tree status drift

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--apply` | false | repair drifted statuses |
| `--plan` | — | limit to one plan slug or id |

Examples:

```bash
devdb plan reconcile                          # show drift in every plan
devdb plan reconcile --plan my-plan             # drift in one plan
devdb plan reconcile --plan my-plan --apply     # repair the drift

Note: there is no --dry-run flag. The verb's natural mode is dry-run; pass
--apply to repair. (Gotcha that bit triage on 2026-06-24.)
```

#### `devdb plan scaffold`

```text

```

Create plan skeleton and HTML artifact

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--body` | — | plan description |
| `--milestones` | 4 | number of milestones |
| `--mode` | implement | design\|implement |
| `--output` | — | HTML artifact path (default: docs/<slug>-implementation-plan.html) |
| `--skip-acceptance` | false | omit default acceptance criteria |
| `--slug` | — | plan slug (auto from title) |
| `--with-implement-items` | false | also create one auto 'Implement/Design Milestone N' item per milestone (legacy shape; default off) |

#### `devdb plan show`

```text

```

Show plan header and milestones

#### `devdb plan status`

```text
status [SLUG_OR_ID]
```

With a plan reference, counts that plan's items only. Without one (or with --global), counts every plan item in the ledger — the fleet dashboard view.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--global` | false | aggregate across all plans even when a plan reference is given |

#### `devdb plan tree`

```text

```

Plan hierarchy

### devdb plan acceptance

Acceptance criteria

| Verb | Summary |
|---|---|
| `add` | Add acceptance criterion |
| `backfill` | Backfill acceptance criteria from a Markdown spec |
| `list` | List acceptance criteria |
| `meet` | Mark acceptance criterion met |

##### `devdb plan acceptance add`

```text
add CRITERION
```

Add acceptance criterion

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ordinal` | 0 | criterion order (auto when 0) |
| `--plan-item` | — | plan item id |

##### `devdb plan acceptance backfill`

Backfill acceptance criteria from a Markdown spec

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--milestone` | — | milestone heading (e.g. M1) |
| `--spec` | — | path to Markdown spec file |

##### `devdb plan acceptance list`

List acceptance criteria, for one plan item (--plan-item) or for a whole
plan (--plan). This is the read verb the group never had: the only way
to see criteria used to be `plan item show`.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--open` | false | only criteria that are not met yet (with --plan) |
| `--plan` | — | plan id or slug |
| `--plan-item` | — | plan item id (prefix ok) |

##### `devdb plan acceptance meet`

```text
meet ID
```

Mark acceptance criterion met

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--evidence` | — | evidence note or commit |

Examples:

```bash
devdb plan acceptance meet <criterion-id> --evidence "<commit-or-note>"

Writes inside storage.WithTx, so it gets the same bounded, jittered
SQLITE_BUSY retry as every other write path: meeting criteria in parallel
from separate processes is safe. The old sequential-discipline rule was a
workaround for MeetAcceptance running a bare Exec and is retired.
```

| `--plan` | — | plan id |
| `--step` | — | optional step label within the phase; renders as "[phase.step] title" |

##### `devdb plan item close`

```text
close ID
```

Close a plan item when acceptance is met

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--evidence` | — | closure evidence (e.g. commit sha) |
| `--note` | — | free-form annotation prepended to the status_log entry |

Examples:

```bash
devdb plan item close <id> --evidence "<commit-or-note>"
devdb plan item close <id-prefix> --note "free-form annotation" --evidence "<commit>"

Closes the item and, when it is the last open item in its milestone or
plan, auto-cascades the parent statuses to done in a single transaction.
Meet each acceptance criterion first — see skills/devdb/SKILL.md "Closure ritual".
```

## Global flags

Accepted by every command.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` | false | expand list limits on read commands |
| `--db` | — | database path (default: .devdb/development.db) |
| `--json` | false | machine-readable JSON output |
| `--model-id` | — | model id recorded on rows this invocation writes (default: $DEVDB_MODEL_ID, else "unknown") |
| `--repo` | — | repository root (default: auto-detect) |
| `--repo-root` | — | alias for --repo (deprecated; for legacy muscle memory) |
| `--verbose` | false | include diagnostic detail |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | general failure |
| 2 | usage error (unknown command, bad flag, invalid filter value) |
| 3 | entity not found |
| 4 | schema error |
| 5 | invalid value (e.g. rejected `arch add` topic) |

Write commands print a bare entity id on stdout; human-facing detail goes to stderr, so `id=$(devdb plan create ...)` stays clean.
